what_its_for: This combination medicine is used in women who have gone through menopause. It helps relieve hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, and other symptoms caused by lower hormone levels. It may also help prevent thinning of the bones (osteoporosis). It contains two hormones: an estrogen (conjugated estrogens) and a progestin (medroxyprogesterone).
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor told you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time every day so it is easier to remember. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the lowest dose that works for you. A common starting dose is one tablet once a day. For Prempro, you take one combination tablet every day. For Premphase, you take an estrogen-only tablet for the first 14 days of the month, then a combination tablet for the last 14 days. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary from person to person.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose as normal. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking while taking this medicine, as it greatly increases the risk of serious side effects like blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Limit alcohol, as it can increase estrogen levels and raise the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because some products (like St. John's Wort, certain antibiotics, and seizure medicines) can make this medicine less effective or cause harmful interactions. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: chest pain, pain in your arm or jaw, sudden shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness or numbness on one side of your body, pain or swelling in your legs, unusual vaginal bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, lumps in your breast, or signs of an allergic reaction like rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also call your doctor if you have ongoing mood changes, depression, or side effects that bother you. Regular check-ups and breast exams are very important while on this medicine.
when_it_works: Many women notice improvement in hot flashes and night sweats within a few weeks of starting this medicine, often within 2 to 4 weeks. Vaginal symptoms may take a little longer to improve. For bone protection, the medicine works over a longer period of time. Talk to your doctor about how long you should stay on this treatment — it is usually reviewed every year.
special_populations: This medicine is NOT for use in men or children. It is only for women who have gone through menopause. Women with a history of breast cancer, blood clots, stroke, heart attack, liver problems, or unexplained vaginal bleeding should not take this medicine. Older women may have a higher risk of serious side effects. Tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medicine. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy. If you think you may be pregnant, stop taking it and contact your doctor right away.
